name: FormTray
title: one dock icon to switch, launch and arrange every FormAI app
summary: FormTray is a launcher and switching station for the 23 FormAI apps: one icon, five views on system glass, rebindable hotkeys, and no network access.
lede: FormTray is a launcher and switching station for the 23 FormAI apps. You pin one icon instead of twenty-three; click it in the Dock and a Stack pops up above it, or press a hotkey and the Switcher, Apps panel, open-app cards or Widgets board appears in one frame. It opens and switches apps only; installing and updating stay in FormPortal.
checks: Shows the whole Form family from one registry in five views: Switcher, Stack, Apps, Windows and Widgets.
Uses real system glass: NSGlassEffectView on macOS 26, vibrancy on older macOS, acrylic on Windows and solid themed panels on Linux.
Reads each app's own name and icon from its bundle, desktop entry or executable every time it looks for apps.

facts.dd: Five views plus Settings, all reading the same state
Rust (formtray-core, formtray-cli) with a Tauri 2 shell and a vanilla TypeScript and Vite interface with zero runtime dependencies
23 apps from one registry, 3 operating systems
JSON files under the OS config folder; ./formtray cli where prints the path

chapters.title: One engine, five ways in
chapters.text: Switcher is a Cmd+Tab-style strip, Stack a Dock folder grid, Apps a searchable panel with categories, Windows cards for open apps and Widgets a board you arrange. Pins, recents and running dots always agree.

chapters.title: Hotkeys that do not fight the system
chapters.text: Defaults are chosen per OS around the reserved chords. Click a hotkey in Settings and press a new chord; FormTray refuses a chord the system or another FormTray action already uses, and Default puts the original back.

chapters.title: A board you arrange
chapters.text: The Widgets board holds app tiles in three sizes, groups of apps that open as a pop-over, and a FormPortal Updates tile counting what FormPortal has already seen. The Updates tile reads FormPortal's files and never fetches.

features.title: Five views
features.text: Every view reads the same state, so pins, recents and running dots agree.
bullets: Switcher: a Cmd+Tab-style strip
Stack: a Dock folder grid
Apps: a searchable panel with categories
Windows: cards for the apps that are open
Widgets: a board you arrange

features.title: Real system glass
features.text: macOS 26 gets a native glass material, older macOS vibrancy, Windows acrylic and Linux solid themed panels.
bullets: Older macOS gets vibrancy
Windows gets acrylic
Linux gets solid themed panels

features.title: Hotkeys
features.text: Per-OS defaults chosen around each system's reserved chords, with clashes refused, not ignored.
bullets: Switcher: Option + Tab on macOS, Alt + ` on Windows and Linux
Views 1 to 5 on a chord per OS
Rebind any hotkey in Settings
On Wayland, bind formtray --view apps (or switcher, stack, windows, widgets) in your desktop's keyboard settings

features.title: Finds apps however they were built
features.text: FormTray reads FormPortal's install record first, and each app carries every bundle identifier and name it has shipped under.
bullets: Names and icons come from the apps themselves
Bundled icons are only a fallback for apps that are not installed
On macOS, a family app FormTray has never heard of appears under More

features.title: Widgets
features.text: A board you arrange with tiles and groups.
bullets: App tiles in three sizes
Groups of apps that open as a pop-over
A FormPortal Updates tile that reads FormPortal's files and never fetches

features.title: Idles in the menu bar
features.text: Once opened, FormTray waits until a hotkey, the Dock icon or the menu bar calls it.
bullets: Open at login is off by default
The menu bar icon is a 3x3 grid
The menu opens your pinned apps directly

features.title: Command line
features.text: The engine runs without a window through formtray-cli.
bullets: list, open, quit, hotkeys, hotkey <action> <chord>, updates and where
./formtray cli list
./formtray cli where prints the preferences folder

features.title: Never touches the network
features.text: FormTray reads, but never writes, FormPortal's installed.json and catalog/apps.json.
bullets: Preferences and usage are local JSON files
Vite dev server on localhost only (port 5610)
FORMPORTAL_ROOT overrides FormPortal's location

features.title: Adding a FormAI app
features.text: Add one entry to core/data/apps.json with its id, form* display name, category, hue, fallback icon and bundle identifiers and names.
bullets: Put a 256 px fallback icon in frontend/public/apps/
No code changes are needed
List an id under excluded to hold an app back

topics.title: Hotkeys
topics.text: The README gives the default Switcher hotkey, Option + Tab on macOS and Alt + ` on Windows and Linux (X11), and how to bind each view on Wayland.

topics.title: Desktop builds
topics.text: ./build_app makes a macOS .app and .dmg, Linux deb, rpm and appimage packages, and on Windows build_app.bat makes an msi and an NSIS setup.

topics.title: Where things live
topics.text: core holds the engine and registry, cli the command line, src-tauri the window shell and frontend the views.

topics.title: Adding a FormAI app
topics.text: One entry in core/data/apps.json and a fallback icon add an app with no code changes.

topics.title: Releases
topics.text: FormTray builds nothing in its repository; pushing a compile_vX.Y.Z branch has formcompiler build the bundles and draft a release.

items: The About box and the installers name NodeAgentc, Inc. and the licence
First release built end to end by formcompiler for macOS, Linux and Windows
A Linux desktop entry counts only when its program exists
Test suite for the registry, Linux platform layer and settings, run in CI

shots_wanted.what: The Apps panel listing the family with search
shots_wanted.how: Run ./formtray, open http://localhost:5610 in a browser and press 3 to switch to the Apps view; type in the search box.
In the same browser view press Cmd or Ctrl + , to open Settings and scroll to the hotkeys.

shots_wanted.what: The Widgets board with tiles and a group
shots_wanted.how: Press 5 for the Widgets view and arrange a few app tiles, including a group.
Press 1 for the Switcher view and use the arrow keys to move the selection.
